# overview

# overview

Section `overview` — marker `00`, position 1 of 24 in the guide.
Generated from `index.html`; prose quoted, counts from the inventory, no URL (the project is
private until v1.0). See `index.json` for the whole set and the shared statement.

## What the guide says

A token-driven interface system for three kinds of page: a landing page that has to persuade, a documentation site that has to explain, and a dashboard that has to be read at speed. Ink-dark by default, daylight-ready by design, and built around the one curve that makes a map a map: the isoline.

only the names are here, because the same figure in two files is how a document
starts disagreeing with itself.

- `.c-btn`

# Six rules that break every tie.

# Six rules that break every tie.

Section `principles` — marker `01`, position 2 of 24 in the guide.
Generated from `index.html`; prose quoted, counts from the inventory, no URL (the project is
private until v1.0). See `index.json` for the whole set and the shared statement.

## What the guide says

When a decision is not obvious, these decide it. They are ordered by how often they come up.

In a dark chart, elevation is expressed by surface lightness and a single hairline. Shadows are reserved for things that genuinely float: menus, dialogs, toasts.

Eighty-five percent of the interface is neutral. Tidal marks action and success, Plasma marks live data, Clay marks failure. Nothing is coloured decoratively.

Size and weight alone leave a page flat. Generous space around the thing that matters does the same job, without adding another colour or border.

IBM Plex Mono is reserved for data, coordinates, labels and code. If it is prose, it is set in IBM Plex Sans. The split makes machine-read data instantly distinguishable.

A control shows the action it performs, and the state it is in, before you touch it. Sort arrows, delta arrows, a copy button that becomes a tick. Affordance here means obvious.

A landing page, a documentation site and a dashboard read as the same product: the same tokens, the same type scale, the same hairline. Only the density changes.

## Subsections

- Lighter, not shadowed
- Colour is a signal
- Space carries the hierarchy
- Mono means "machine"
- Obvious, not guessed
- One system, three surfaces

# Colour, in five families and a neutral ramp.

# Colour, in five families and a neutral ramp.

Section `colour` — marker `02`, position 3 of 24 in the guide.
Generated from `index.html`; prose quoted, counts from the inventory, no URL (the project is
private until v1.0). See `index.json` for the whole set and the shared statement.

## What the guide says

Every value is defined in OKLCH so lightness steps read evenly. Neutrals are tinted toward the brand hue — never pure grey. Themes are semantic: swap the semantic layer and the primitives stay put.

What a component asks for, not what a colour happens to be. The same role resolves differently in each theme.

Five elevation steps. In dark mode, higher means lighter — never a heavier shadow.

For density, catchments and isoline bands. Seven stops, one hue, rising lightness.

For bearing, aspect and phase. Eight stops, equal lightness, hue carries the encoding, wraps seamlessly from 360° back to 0°.

For hazard, density and continuous surfaces. Six stops, non-monotonic lightness — hot, not ordered.

## Subsections

- Semantic roles
- Surfaces & text
- Sequential scale
- Cyclic scale
- Heat scale

# Two families, one superfamily.

# Two families, one superfamily.

Section `type` — marker `03`, position 4 of 24 in the guide.
Generated from `index.html`; prose quoted, counts from the inventory, no URL (the project is
private until v1.0). See `index.json` for the whole set and the shared statement.

## What the guide says

IBM Plex Sans Condensed sets the display voice; IBM Plex Sans carries body copy; IBM Plex Mono is reserved for anything the machine produced. Contrast comes from proportion, not from mixing unrelated typefaces.

Contour lines 0123456789

Backend-less routing

16.4 km · 19 min

Body copy is capped at 68 characters and set at 1.65 leading — looser than the default, because light-on-dark text needs more air.

# Motion that decelerates, never bounces.

# Motion that decelerates, never bounces.

Section `motion` — marker `05`, position 6 of 24 in the guide.
Generated from `index.html`; prose quoted, counts from the inventory, no URL (the project is
private until v1.0). See `index.json` for the whole set and the shared statement.

## What the guide says

Exponential easing for entrances, tight linear curves for continuous motion, and a hard stop for anything the user did not ask for. Every animation respects prefers-reduced-motion.

prefers-reduced-motion is an operating-system setting, so it is not the mechanism WCAG 2.2.2 asks for: a reader cannot reach it for one part of one page, and most have never opened it. [data-motion] is the page's own switch. paused holds every animation in its scope on the frame it is on — a spinner stays mid-rotation and still means working. running overrides the media query; leaving the attribute unset gives the choice back to the system.

The same attribute is the seam for content that updates on a timer: when a live region stops being live, the producer that polls it should set data-motion="paused" too, because 2.2.2 covers auto-updating information, not only motion.

Hover, focus and press. Anything that must feel instantaneous.

State changes on surfaces: border, background, transform.

Entrances, reveals and anything that moves the eye across a gap.

## Subsections

- Motion a reader can stop

# Forms

# Forms

Section `forms` — marker `07`, position 8 of 24 in the guide.
Generated from `index.html`; prose quoted, counts from the inventory, no URL (the project is
private until v1.0). See `index.json` for the whole set and the shared statement.

## What the guide says

Controls sized for the hand and the keyboard. Every input has a visible label, a visible focus state and room for an error message that explains, not scolds. A select keeps its native option list: the platform draws that, so it follows the operating system's theme rather than the page's.

Autocomplete input with keyboard navigation. Type to filter, arrow keys to navigate, Enter to select, Escape to close.

- Combobox

# Surfaces

# Surfaces

Section `surfaces` — marker `09`, position 10 of 24 in the guide.
Generated from `index.html`; prose quoted, counts from the inventory, no URL (the project is
private until v1.0). See `index.json` for the whole set and the shared statement.

## What the guide says

Cards are for things that are independently actionable. Information that only belongs to its group does not get a container — it gets space and a rule.

Route calculation runs in single-digit milliseconds once the tile graph is built.

Catchment areas and travel-time bands, with inner breaks for context.

Every result exports as GeoJSON, ready for QGIS, ArcGIS or a paper map.

Used once per page. If two plates meet, one of them should be a card.

Borderless, indexed, ruled at the top. The counter-move to the card grid.

No routing server, no third-party API, no latency tax.

The same query always returns the same engine and result.

The end of the page: the brand, a line about what this is, and the links that stay reachable.

A design system for spatial interfaces. One set of rules for three surfaces.

Scroll container with content-visibility for performance. Virtualization logic is the consumer's responsibility — this provides the CSS containment and scroll behavior.

## Subsections

- Millisecond routing
- Isolines, built in
- GeoJSON out
- A raised surface for hero content
- Feature blocks
- Foundations
- Components

# Navigation

# Navigation

Section `navigation` — marker `10`, position 11 of 24 in the guide.
Generated from `index.html`; prose quoted, counts from the inventory, no URL (the project is
private until v1.0). See `index.json` for the whole set and the shared statement.

## What the guide says

Tabs for peer views, segmented controls for exclusive choices, a toolbar for map-level actions. Each one announces its state to assistive technology.

The bar that holds the brand, the section links and the actions. It sticks to the top of the page; below 48 rem the links move into a drawer.

Handles high-degree road networks with predictable memory use.

Bidirectional A* with a geographic heuristic. Fastest for point-to-point queries where both endpoints are known.

Adaptive barrier SSSP. Scales to very large networks by keeping the frontier small.

The headings of the page being read, with the current one marked. The guide's own rail is the same idea, numbered and built from the page.

On this page

# Feedback

# Feedback

Section `feedback` — marker `11`, position 12 of 24 in the guide.
Generated from `index.html`; prose quoted, counts from the inventory, no URL (the project is
private until v1.0). See `index.json` for the whole set and the shared statement.

## What the guide says

Every state the interface can be in has a component: empty, loading, error, done. Each one teaches rather than decorates.

Tile cache is empty

The first route will fetch and parse every tile in range.

Snapshot ahead of coverage

No road data within 120 m. Choose a closer endpoint.

Route failed

Every engine returned no safe path between these points.

Streaming live

312 walkers are moving. The flow network updates as they go.

Exported

catchment-15min.geojson is ready to open in QGIS.

No waypoints yet

Pick a start and an end on the map, then reveal the desire lines.

Progress drawn as elevation rings rather than a bar — the system's own shape language applied to a data component.

## Subsections

- Loading
- Empty state
- Contour meter
- Progress & toasts

# Overlays

# Overlays

Section `overlays` — marker `12`, position 13 of 24 in the guide.
Generated from `index.html`; prose quoted, counts from the inventory, no URL (the project is
private until v1.0). See `index.json` for the whole set and the shared statement.

## What the guide says

Dialogs for decisions that need focus, a command palette for the whole system, a drawer for drill-down, and tooltips that appear on interest rather than on click.

Hover or focus the panel to strengthen the grip.

Content behind the scrim.

The classic map-tool panel: a scrollable body, a fixed footer, and a grip that collapses it on small screens.

Walking instinct lab

A drill-down that slides over the content without losing it. Pinned to the viewport in an app; inline here, so it can be read next to the thing it describes.

Why this route

Crossing at the canal lock costs less than the detour around it.

Modal dialog, hint tooltip, command palette and the toast live region. These ship as overlay primitives; the demo instances live in the page footer.

- Side sheet

- Drawer

# Data display

# Data display

Section `data` — marker `13`, position 14 of 24 in the guide.
Generated from `index.html`; prose quoted, counts from the inventory, no URL (the project is
private until v1.0). See `index.json` for the whole set and the shared statement.

## What the guide says

Numbers are set in mono with tabular figures so columns align. Readouts use dotted rules instead of boxes, which keeps dense data calm — and no two series are ever separated by hue alone.

The friction cost of each surface, and where people end up walking anyway.

Walking resistance

Where people choose to walk

Stable release

Deterministic engine selection, GeoJSON export, MapLibre control.

Isolines and catchment analysis

IsoPHAST integrated, with inner pretty-breaks for context.

Public beta

Tile parsing and graph construction moved fully client-side.

Eight hues separate by hue, not by lightness — so a line also carries a dash pattern, and the legend previews that pattern. No chart asks the reader to tell two colours apart, and every series clears 3:1 against every surface it can be drawn on (canvas, canvas-sunken, surface-1/2/3, surface-raised), in both themes.

Bars for magnitude, one hue per series. The same plot, axis and tooltip vocabulary as the line chart — only the mark changes.

2D density with isoline overlay — the signature motif as function. Marching squares over a real field, same algorithm as the generator. No other design system ships this.

Add data-chart-export to a chart to get an SVG download button. Exports vector graphics for reports and presentations.

A panel always says where it stands. Empty is not an error, live is not idle, and the error state says what to do next.

Nothing to show yet

No isolines for this catchment.

Streaming

Receiving routes.

Source unreachable

Tile server did not answer.

What just happened, newest first. The dot carries the severity; the time stays in mono so a column of them still scans.

Direction is drawn as well as named — an arrow, a word, and a colour that agrees.

The contract a third party follows. A component is a CSS block in the right layer, a specimen in the guide, and a snippet the tool extracts.

A migration aid: the names a consumer may already know, and the Contour class that replaces them.

## Subsections

- Engine readout
- Walking resistance
- Engine comparison
- Release timeline
- Chart series
- Bar chart
- Contour plot
- Chart export
- Panel states
- Activity
- Deltas
- How to add a component
- Rename table (legacy → Contour)

Shown — same markup, wider profile.

# Documentation

# Documentation

Section `docs` — marker `15`, position 16 of 24 in the guide.
Generated from `index.html`; prose quoted, counts from the inventory, no URL (the project is
private until v1.0). See `index.json` for the whole set and the shared statement.

## What the guide says

The parts that make a manual usable: a callout that holds a rule, a list of steps that holds an order, a diff that holds a change, and a pager that holds the way out.

Five tones. Each carries an icon and a word, so the meaning survives a monochrome print and a reader who cannot tell red from green.

Note

Tile URLs are parsed once and cached for the rest of the session.

Tip

Pre-warm the tile cache before the first query for the fastest start.

Caution

Avoid routing on a carriageway — the graph has no turn restrictions there.

Unsupported

Isoline extraction needs a time-based weight; other costs cannot be contoured.

New in 1.0

Delta-stepping is now the default engine for weighted graphs — 4× faster than the previous selector, with the same results.

The clearest way to teach a convention is to show both outcomes, side by side.

Do

Name the axis a number is measured on. 7 ms median is a fact; 7 is a rumour.

Don't

Drop the unit or the comparison period. A delta without a baseline cannot be argued with.

A numbered procedure. The number is a waypoint, not an ornament — the rule and the connector between numbers both say the order is not optional.

Any vector tileset with a routable profile works. Contour reads the standard schema, so there is nothing to pre-process.

Give it a start and an end. The default radius of 50 m covers most addresses; raise it only for rural geometry.

You get geometry, cost and the engine that produced them — enough to draw the line and to explain the number beside it.

One snippet, three package managers. The choice is remembered per group, so a reader who prefers pnpm is not nagged on every page.

A single command with a copy button — the most-used component on any documentation site.

ESM only, 42 kB gzipped, no peer dependencies beyond MapLibre.

For changelogs and migration guides. The removed line and its replacement sit on adjacent rows, so the eye can compare them without counting.

A version picker in the header, and a banner when the reader is on an old one.

A project tree in a code panel, with the file under the cursor marked.

Contour ships no syntax highlighter (zero runtime dependencies); highlighting is the consumer's. src/css/hljs.css maps highlight.js token classes onto Contour tokens, so a consumer who runs that highlighter gets code that matches the system's palette in both themes. It sets colour only — never layout, never font-family. Load it after the library's own stylesheet.

The way out of a long page, at the foot of it. Both links are real links, so they survive a right-click and a middle click.

# Affordances, made visible.

# Affordances, made visible.

Section `affordances` — marker `18`, position 19 of 24 in the guide.
Generated from `index.html`; prose quoted, counts from the inventory, no URL (the project is
private until v1.0). See `index.json` for the whole set and the shared statement.

## What the guide says

An element should look like what it does before anyone touches it. Each interactive class in the system carries a signifier — a shape, a handle, an arrow — that announces its behaviour. Nothing is implied by position alone, and nothing is left to be guessed at.

Button

Filled, raised, pill-shaped with a shadow that implies height. It lifts on hover and presses on activation.

Switch

A knob that slides. Position carries the state, so the meaning survives greyscale.

Slider

A track with a filled portion and a round thumb. The fill shows the value without a number.

Checkbox

A square that fills with a tick. Round for radio, square for multiple.

Filter pill

Names its key and value, and carries a visible remove control. Nothing is removable by guesswork.

Drag handle

Six dots. The near-universal signifier for reordering, and it changes the cursor on hover.

Sortable column

An arrow appears on hover and locks to a direction once sorted. The sort state is announced to assistive technology.

Disclosure

A chevron that rotates. A plus becomes a cross when open, so the control reads as reversible.

Copy

The icon becomes a tick for a moment. The result is visible without a toast and without reading a label.

Link

Underlined in prose and coloured outside it. A link never looks like a button.

Disabled

Dimmed, with a not-allowed cursor. Disabled is a state, never a silent dead end.

Cursor

Every clickable thing declares its cursor — pointer, grab, col-resize. The cheapest signifier there is.

Hidden content revealed on toggle.

This action cannot be undone.

RTL specimen — chevron flips to the inline-start side.

The spatial dashboard skeleton: an app shell, a map area with floating panels, a footer for charts, and the containers that fill them.

.c-row — horizontal flex, items centered

.c-stack — vertical, gap scales with --space-md

.c-cluster — wrapping, for tags and chips

.c-box — padded container, size variants

Default box (md padding)

.c-map-slot — map chrome container

.c-map-panel — floating panel over the map

Top-right panel

Bottom-left panel

.c-map-footer — bottom bar for charts and tables

Cell 1

Cell 2

Cell 3

.c-container — fixed (fit content) + scrollable (fill space)

Fixed container

Fits its content, stays put.

Scrollable container

Fills remaining space

And scrolls if needed

More content here

Even more content

Main content area

.c-app / .c-app-body — application shell

Sidebar

# Three shells, one system.

# Three shells, one system.

Section `recipes` — marker `19`, position 20 of 24 in the guide.
Generated from `index.html`; prose quoted, counts from the inventory, no URL (the project is
private until v1.0). See `index.json` for the whole set and the shared statement.

## What the guide says

Contour covers landing pages, documentation sites and technical dashboards. The components are shared; the composition, density and type scale change. Below are all three, rendered live.

A page whose only job is to earn a click. Generous type, one primary action, and a hero that shows the product rather than describing it. The contour field runs full-bleed behind everything.

Compute routes and isolines from OpenMapTiles entirely client-side. No routing server, no third-party API, no data leaving the device.

No routing infrastructure to size, monitor or pay for. The deployment footprint stays flat.

Millisecond-scale responses with no round trip, so the map feels like a surface rather than a request.

Routing, isolines, a MapLibre control and GeoJSON export in one package.

A reading surface where the URL is the state. A navigation tree on the left, a measured prose column in the middle, an on-this-page rail on the right. Every entry is a real link, so it all works without JavaScript.

Getting started

Install the package, point it at a tile source, and compute your first route. Four lines, no server.

The package ships ESM and type definitions. No peer dependencies beyond MapLibre, and none of them are required for the core API.

Call route() with a source, a destination and a tile URL. It returns the geometry, the cost and the engine that produced them.

Tile preparation dominates

The first call fetches and parses every tile in range. The search itself takes milliseconds — budget for the graph, not the query.

On this page

A scanning surface. Density is the feature: comfortable by default, one toggle for compact. Every panel reports its own state, and chart colours come from a dedicated token layer so series stay distinguishable.

Last 7 days · all profiles

By route volume

48 rows · sorted by latency

# Two themes, one cascade.

# Two themes, one cascade.

Section `theming` — marker `21`, position 22 of 24 in the guide.
Generated from `index.html`; prose quoted, counts from the inventory, no URL (the project is
private until v1.0). See `index.json` for the whole set and the shared statement.

## What the guide says

The color-scheme property on :root is the only switch. Every semantic token resolves through light-dark(), so the palette follows the OS by default — and CSS never depends on JavaScript to be readable.

Deeper surfaces, one hairline, no shadows. Designed for long sessions in a dim room and for maps that need to glow against the page.

A paper-white chart with ink text. The same five families, re-stepped for contrast on light surfaces — not an inversion of the dark palette.

Stored in localStorage, applied before first paint.

Page-level morphing via the View Transitions API. Add data-view-transition with a --view-transition-name to morph elements across navigations. Falls back gracefully in browsers without support.

Morph a card between two states using the View Transitions API. The card's view-transition-name links the before and after states.

Compact state

Expanded state with more content and a wider layout.

A card and a dialog share one view-transition-name, so the card morphs into the dialog (and back) instead of cross-fading. The name is the only link between the two surfaces.

Compact surface that expands into a dialog.

Expanded surface reached by morphing the card.

A small preview surface morphs into its full detail surface. Both carry the same view-transition-name; the browser interpolates size, position and content between them.

Thumbnail

Full surface with the complete content and a wider layout.

# Install

# Install

Section `install` — marker `22`, position 23 of 24 in the guide.
Generated from `index.html`; prose quoted, counts from the inventory, no URL (the project is
private until v1.0). See `index.json` for the whole set and the shared statement.

## What the guide says

Plain CSS in src/, one entry point, no build step and no runtime. Link it and start using the class names.

Optional progressive enhancement. Load contour-wc.js after ds.css to use contour-btn, contour-card, and 320+ other custom elements that generate their scaffolding from attributes. Light-DOM elements (contour-*) use the cascade directly; shadow-DOM elements (contour-shadow-*) ship slots and adopted stylesheets for encapsulation. Interactive blocks (tabs, combobox, tree, menu, segmented, dialog, tag, filter-pill, install, code, pagination) wire their own keyboard behaviour and dispatch contour:* CustomEvents (contour:select, contour:change, contour:remove, contour:copy, contour:page, contour:close, contour:theme-change), so they work standalone. Modifier attributes (variant, size, color) apply to both layers from one list, and attribute changes re-render without losing authored content.

Slotted content in the shadow root.

# Web components

# Web components

Section `webcomponents` — marker `23`, position 24 of 24 in the guide.
Generated from `index.html`; prose quoted, counts from the inventory, no URL (the project is
private until v1.0). See `index.json` for the whole set and the shared statement.

## What the guide says

Optional progressive enhancement. Load contour-wc.js after ds.css to use contour-* and contour-shadow-* custom elements that generate their scaffolding from attributes. Light-DOM elements use the cascade directly; shadow-DOM elements ship slots and adopted stylesheets for encapsulation.

Where each shape of the markup lives: §04–§22 show every block as the CSS an author writes by hand, and this section shows the same blocks as elements that generate it. The division is deliberate, not a migration left half-done. The raw markup is the contract a consumer copies, and it works with no script at all; this layer is the optional enhancement over that same contract, so a page can drop it and lose nothing but its attributes.

Reactivity: every component extends ContourBase, which snapshots the author's nodes and class on first connect. An attribute change restores that snapshot, re-runs render(), and re-wires behaviour via enhance(), so authored content and listeners survive while generated nodes are rebuilt. Form values are preserved across a re-render; render bodies use ensure() for update-or-create reactivity.

Composition: components never reach into one another. A host composes by nesting or slotted content, and interactive components emit bubbling contour:* CustomEvents (contour:change, contour:select, contour:copy, contour:remove, contour:page, contour:open/ contour:close) that a parent handles without coupling to internals. Shadow wrappers adopt the document's same-origin sheets once and share one parsed stylesheet across instances.

One card, two ways to change it. Writing three attributes in turn rebuilds the card three times; the same three writes inside batch() rebuild it once. The count is the element's own renderCount, not a number this page keeps, so it cannot drift from what the layer did.

Toggle attributes live and watch the component re-render. The alert's variant and the kpi's value are driven by the controls below; no page-level state is kept.

contour-input, contour-select, contour-check and contour-switch participate in a native form via ElementInternals: their values are submitted, validated and reset like native controls. Submit the form below to see the FormData it produces.

Interactive components emit bubbling contour:* CustomEvents on the host, so a parent handles them without coupling to internals. The menu below emits contour:select; the pagination emits contour:page.

Authored content survives re-renders.

Slotted content in the shadow root.

Dialog body content.

Dialog body content.

Content behind the scrim.
